STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company leases the land underlying the Wyndham Palm Springs hotel pursuant to a sub-lease agreement with an initial term ending December 2059, with
the right to extend the term an additional 25 years. Annual rent due under the lease is the greater of base rent or percentage rent. Base rent for the years 2005 through 2009 is approximately $0.9 million. Base rent increases every five years over
the remaining term of the lease by the increase in the CPI over that same five-year period; however, the increase in base rent every five years will not be increased by an amount greater than 30% of the base rent for the preceding five-year period.
Annual percentage rent is equal to the sum of 4% of rooms gross receipts, 2% of food and beverage gross receipts, and 10% of tenant rentals. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Management Agreements</I>&#151;As of December&nbsp;31, 2005, the Company&#146;s hotel properties operated pursuant to long-term agreements with seven
management companies, including Crestline Hotels&nbsp;&amp; Resorts, Inc. (13 hotels), Marriott International, Inc. (3 hotels), Hyatt Corporation (2 hotels), McKibbon Hotel Management, Inc. (2&nbsp;hotels), Hilton Hotels Corporation (1 hotel), Sage
Hospitality Resources (1 hotel), and Grubarges Gesti&oacute;n Hotelera Mexicana SA de CV (1 resort). Each management company receives a base management fee generally between 2% and 4% of hotel revenues. The management companies are also eligible to
receive an incentive management fee if hotel operating income, as defined in the management agreements, exceeds certain performance thresholds. The incentive management fee is generally calculated as a percentage of hotel operating income after the
Company has received a priority return on its investment in the hotel. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2"><I>Franchise Agreements</I>&#151;As of December&nbsp;31, 2005, 15 of the Company&#146;s 23 hotel properties operated pursuant to franchise agreements from national hotel companies. Pursuant to the franchise agreements, the Company pays a
royalty fee generally between 4% and 5% of room revenues, plus additional fees for marketing, central reservation systems, and other franchisor costs that amount to between 3% and 4% of room revenues from the hotels. Six of the Company&#146;s 23
hotel properties, which include the Hyatt Regency Savannah hotel, the Hyatt Regency Wind Watch Long Island hotel, the Dallas/Fort Worth Airport Marriott hotel, the Courtyard Boston Tremont hotel, the Courtyard Denver Airport hotel, and the Hilton
Boston Back Bay hotel, are managed by Hyatt Corporation, Marriott International, Inc., or Hilton Hotels Corporation. The management agreements for these six hotel properties allow the hotel property to operate under the respective brand. With
respect to the Company&#146;s other two hotel properties, the management agreement for the Barcel&oacute; Tucancun Beach resort allows the hotel property to operate under the Barcel&oacute; brand and The Churchill hotel operates as an independent
hotel. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Property Improvement Reserves</I>&#151;Pursuant to
its management, franchise and loan agreements, the Company is required to establish a property improvement reserve for each hotel to cover the cost of replacing furniture, fixtures and equipment at the hotels. Contributions to the property
improvement reserve are based on a percentage of gross revenues or receipts at each hotel. The Company is generally required to contribute between 3% and 5% of gross revenues each month over the term of the agreements. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Litigation</I>&#151;The Company is not involved in any material litigation
nor, to its knowledge, is any material litigation threatened against the Company. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Subsequent Events </B></FONT></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On January&nbsp;6, 2006, the Company completed a $35 million financing secured by the Westin Princeton at Forrestal Village hotel. The loan bears a fixed
annual interest rate of 5.97% and matures on February&nbsp;1, 2013. Principal payments will commence in February 2007 and will be based on a 30-year amortization period. The loan agreement contains a standard provision that requires the loan
servicer to maintain an escrow account over the term of the loan for real estate taxes. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On January&nbsp;18, 2006, the Company&#146;s board of directors declared a cash distribution to Series A preferred stockholders of the Company of record as of February&nbsp;1, 2006. The cash distribution of $.49219
per Series A preferred share was paid on February&nbsp;15, 2006. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2">On February&nbsp;24, 2006, the Company acquired the 673-room Nashville Renaissance hotel in Nashville, Tennessee for approximately $80.2 million. The Company borrowed $10 million under its term loan facility to fund a portion of the
acquisition. The Company entered into a long-term agreement with Marriott International, Inc. to manage the hotel property. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On February&nbsp;24, 2006, the Company extinguished its $100 million term loan facility and completed a separate unsecured revolving credit facility with
a syndicate of banks, including Wells Fargo Bank, N.A., as administration agent. The revolving credit facility provides aggregate revolving loan commitments of up to $150 million with an option to increase the amount of the facility by up to $50
million. The amount that the Company can borrow under the revolving credit facility is based on the value of the Company&#146;s unencumbered hotel properties included in the borrowing base, as defined in the agreement. As of February&nbsp;24, 2006,
the maximum borrowing availability under the facility was approximately $133 million, of which $101 million was drawn down on that date to pay off the term loan facility and pay closing costs on the new facility. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>HIGHLAND HOSPITALITY CORPORATION AND PREDECESSOR </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:-6px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>NOTES TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued) </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Borrowings under the revolving credit facility bear interest at variable rates equal to, at the
Company&#146;s option, either (a)&nbsp;LIBOR, plus a credit spread, or (b)&nbsp;a base rate, plus a credit spread. The base rate in effect on any given day is equal to the higher of (a)&nbsp;the prime rate published by Wells Fargo Bank, N.A., or
(b)&nbsp;the Federal Funds Rate announced by the Federal Reserve Bank, plus 0.5%. The credit spread is reset each quarter based on the Company&#146;s current leverage ratio. The facility agreement contains standard financial covenants, including
certain leverage ratios, coverage ratios, and a minimum tangible net worth. The Company is required to pay an unused fee of 0.20%&nbsp;per annum on the amount of unused capacity under the credit facility. The facility matures on February&nbsp;23,
2009 and has a one-year extension option. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
